noah.p: hi folks, onboarding Q — i requested a staging secret yesterday and noticed it has a monthly rotation policy. my integration test client hard-caches the token. how do we handle rotation for short-lived demos vs. long-lived services?

maria.s: welcome! :wave: short answer: demos should use ephemeral tokens (hours) or KMS-wrapped ciphertexts you unwrap per-run. long-lived services should be migrated to service-roles with auto-rotation and an owner who can respond to rotations.

noah.p: what's the process to convert a demo secret to a service-role later? do i reopen the ticket or file a new one?

ida.l: product owner here — open a new request that asks for a service-role and include the migration plan & who owns it. infra/security will require a revocation runbook before approving prod service roles.

devops-bot: Template for service-role request: `@devops-bot request type=service-role env=prod service=team/redwood-inference reason="migrate demo->service" owners=noah.p,ida.l rotation=auto notify=onrotate` Attach: `migration_plan.md` and `revocation_runbook.md`.

noah.p: got it. another question: what is the breakglass/emergency revocation flow if a key leaks? I want to document it in the runbook.

maria.s: breakglass is manual and audited. Steps: 1) open urgent SEC ticket with subject "breakglass" and tag @oncall-sre, 2) request immediate revoke + rotate, 3) oncall will verify requester via 2FA and phone, 4) infra rotates keys and invalidates sessions, 5) post-mortem & audit entry required. Add phone number in the breakglass ticket.

oncall-sre: confirming — when a breakglass ticket is created we run a temporary global deny for the compromised secret's role, rotate KMS key if used, and issue ephemeral replacement creds. We will also push an incident note to #incidents and kickoff a postmortem.

noah.p: is there an automated way to detect token usage after rotation? I want to ensure my client fails fast rather than silently retrying with old creds.

maria.s: yes — we emit token-revocation logs and have alerting on repeated auth failures from the same client id. Add health-checks to your client to surface auth errors and refresh tokens on 401. We recommend exponential backoff + a hard fail after N attempts.

ida.l: also include SEC ticket ID in PRs when your code changes auth behavior. That helps trace changes during audits.

noah.p: thanks! i'll draft a migration plan and revocation runbook and file the service-role request. any tips for local testing to avoid tripping rotation?

maria.s: use short-lived staging tokens for local tests, and prefer KMS-wrap/unwrap cycle for reproducing production behavior; never persist decrypted secrets to disk. If you need pairing, DM me or @ida.l and we can walk through a sample run.

noah.p: appreciate it, welcome aboard note received. closing this thread once i file the new ticket. :thumbsup:

ida.l: welcome to the team! if you want a 15m chat about owner responsibilities i can schedule one.
